statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 10 while Stress stays elevated at 48; the August expiry close cleared without one-way extension and only a thin futures tail remains before the weekend halt.
recommendation: The closing evidence is consistent with functioning mean reversion: the session produced a full round trip, both extremes were retraced, the index settled below its own open and mid-range, and implied volatility finished at session lows. No danger window is carried inside this horizon, because CME equity index futures halt at 21:00Z and there is no tradable price path again until the Sunday reopen, which falls outside the published 24-hour window. Tail remains well below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Weekly close: the Nasdaq-100 finished +0.33% at 29,308.86 after retracing both session extremes, with futures halting for the weekend against a 5.28% 30-year.
body:
Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% against a 29,213.17 previous close. The index opened at 29,359.60, was sold to a 29,142.44 low, reclaimed the whole decline to a 29,405.12 high and then handed back roughly ninety-six points to close below its own open. NQ September futures are near 29,383.75, about +0.28%, inside a 29,220.00-29,539.00 range and some 155 points beneath their session high with the 21:00Z weekly halt approaching. That sequence is the central Tail evidence and it resolves the one genuinely hour-specific risk carried into this close: the August monthly expiry settled without a one-way extension. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and price finished mid-range rather than pinned at an edge. VIX agrees, closing at 14.89, down 6.00% and near the bottom of a 14.77-15.95 range.

Tail is therefore published at 10, the lowest reading of the session and three points under the 13 that held through the afternoon, because the scheduled-flow premium that justified 16 in the prior hour has now released at the close. It is not a claim that the backdrop improved; it is a statement that the concentrated closing window passed without producing the persistent no-retracement structure that overwhelms mean reversion.

Stress stays elevated at 48 and remains a rates and energy story rather than an equity-structure one. The 10-year finished at 4.74%, up about three and a half basis points and testing 20-month highs, the 30-year at 5.28% is the highest since 2007, and the 2-year at 4.24% is the firmest part of the curve on the day. The Treasury's expanded buyback programme, announced Wednesday and widened Thursday, has not held the long end down. Energy carries the rest: WTI is near $86.88 and Brent $94.07, both closing a second consecutive week of roughly five percent gains with the Strait of Hormuz disruption unresolved and a new US sanctions round on Iran announced. Neither channel transmitted into equity price structure today, but both are why a large recoverable drawdown remains plausible next week.

Internals closed split rather than aligned, which is why the current mode is published as normal rather than trending. Delayed latest-session context shows five of eight megacaps higher with dispersion near 1.8 percentage points, led by Tesla and Alphabet while Nvidia and Apple finished lower, and the semiconductor complex averaged about -0.7% with ARM and Intel the largest drags. The weekly ledger is the wider context: the Nasdaq Composite lost 2.0%, the S&P 500 1.4% and the Dow 0.8%, snapping winning streaks after a bond-driven week that Friday only partly repaired.

Confidence is held at 88. The closing index and futures levels, the day range, VIX, the full Treasury curve, both crude benchmarks, the already-released August flash PMI set, the closing wrap and the forward calendar were all verified directly at this cutoff, and delayed cross-asset context was used only as confirmation. The horizon itself is unusual: from 21:00Z CME equity index futures halt for the weekend, so all twenty-three slots after the current one describe a market with no tradable price path. Scores there step to background floors and Confidence decays with distance from the last observed print rather than because any evidence has been contradicted.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: thirteen hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z and 11:00Z through 19:00Z) while the remaining eleven clock-hours, covering the August 20 US evening and scattered overnight gaps, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours the published Tail held a narrow 12-16 band and the mapped policy state was green throughout, with no hour reaching the watch band. The shape is coherent: Tail sat at 12 through the Asian and European hours while Stress eased from 59 to 54 on an orderly overnight tape, stepped up to 15-16 across the 13:00Z-14:00Z flash-PMI and US-open window where the mode was briefly published as event/whipsaw, then decayed back through 14 to 13 and held there for four consecutive hours as the release was absorbed. The final available hour lifted Tail back to 16, an elevation published specifically for concentrated August monthly expiry flow into the cash close rather than for observed structure. Stress fell in step across the afternoon from 58 to 53 and Confidence climbed steadily from 83 to 88 as more of the session became directly observable.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 10, below every hour of the session, because the expiry close has now cleared without a one-way extension and the scheduled-flow premium published in the prior hour has released. From 21:00Z the horizon changes character completely: CME equity index futures halt for the weekend, so all twenty-three remaining slots describe a market with no tradable price path. Tail steps to a floor of 4-5 there, because the pathological no-retracement sequence this score measures requires a live tape, and the dominant mode is published as normal throughout since a halted market has no structure to characterise. Stress steps down to 35-38, a level representing the standing rate and energy backdrop of a 5.28% 30-year and Brent near $94 rather than any live condition, and it drifts modestly higher across late Saturday as the unpriced weekend interval lengthens into a reopen that must clear accumulated news in a single gap. A gap is a level change rather than a persistent path, so that drift is expressed in Stress and not in Tail. Confidence decays gradually from 88 to 66 with distance from the last observed print rather than because evidence has been contradicted. No scheduled US macro event falls inside the window: the next checkpoints are Monday's Chicago Fed index, then Wednesday's PCE, GDP revision and NVIDIA results, and the Jackson Hole keynote the following Friday, all beyond this horizon.

Stress therefore stays flat here while Tail remains at its floor.
